title: Known geological history is a fragment of the time since the first organism

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Known geological history is a fragment of the time since the first organism

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: The whole history of the world as known from geology is only a small fragment of the time that has elapsed since the first organism, the progenitor of all later forms, came into existence.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: On the Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection, or the Preservation of Favoured Races in the Struggle for Life

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: The whole history of the world, as at present known, although of a length quite incomprehensible by us, will hereafter be recognised as a mere fragment of time, compared with the ages which have elapsed since the first creature, the progenitor of innumerable extinct and living descendants, was created.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci Origin of Species claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Charles Darwin, On the Origin of Species (1st ed., London: John Murray, 1859), Chapter XIV, “Recapitulation and Conclusion”; section “Effects of its adoption on the study of Natural history”. Scope: history of life on earth

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on darwin1859-ch14-09: needs-new-data, resolvability 0.48

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The comparison is conceptually measurable, but its decisive endpoint—the first organism—is not present in current datasets. Existing geochemical constraints do not establish that the missing duration is larger than all known geological history.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Compare the independently estimated age of life's first origin with the duration and completeness of the preserved geological record known to contain life. The claim requires the unrecorded pre-geological interval to greatly exceed the preserved interval.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
No possible fossil sample can directly cover destroyed Hadean crust.

The phrase 'known geological history' changes with discovery.

The time of the first organism is unknown and may predate surviving rocks.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data existence: 0.68
data adequacy: 0.25
discriminating power: 0.42
analysis feasibility: 0.45
operationalizability: 0.52

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Both durations are now numerical, and the Phanerozoic is several times shorter than the interval since the earliest widely discussed evidence of life. That comparison uses public time scales and fossil and rock ages and can be made in days. The soft point is the rhetorical threshold for 'fragment', which keeps discriminating power moderate even though the direction of the inequality is clear.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Compare the radiometric length of the fossiliferous timescale known in 1859, essentially the Phanerozoic, with the time from the earliest evidence of life to the present. The claim is confirmed if that then-known history is a small fraction of post-origin time, and refuted if the two durations are similar under the range of credible dates for first life.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
'Mere fragment' has no numerical cutoff, so a ratio near one sixth can be described in more than one way.

The age of the first organism is a range, from debated early isotopic signals to clearer later fossils.

The phrase 'history of the world as at present known' has to be read as the 1859 fossiliferous timescale, because the geological record known today already includes most of Earth's history.

discriminating power: 0.55
data adequacy: 0.75
operationalizability: 0.6
